# WhyRisk

> WhyRisk is a healthcare risk-prediction and clinical decision-support platform built during a machine-learning internship at Ezitech Institute (Eziline Software House), Islamabad. It combines a Next.js web application, a FastAPI machine-learning service, and a Supabase (PostgreSQL) backend with row-level security.

## What it does

- Predicts diabetes risk with a trained LightGBM model and explains every score with SHAP feature attributions, so the factors behind a score can be inspected instead of trusted blindly.
- Holds patient and doctor records, appointments, and stored risk assessments, with role-based access (patient / doctor / admin) enforced by middleware and database row-level security.
- Computes clinical indicators in code alongside the model score: BMI classification, blood-pressure categorisation, eGFR staging, and cholesterol ratios.
- Includes a symptom checker that is a rule-based heuristic, labelled as such in the product. It is not a trained model.

## The model

- Task: diabetes risk (binary classification) — the only trained model in the system today.
- Dataset: CDC BRFSS 2015 health indicators, balanced 50/50 split file (70,692 records, 21 features, target Diabetes_binary).
- Selected model: LightGBM, AUC-ROC 0.8307 on a stratified held-out test split (80/20). Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were benchmarked against it, with MLflow experiment tracking.
- The 0.8307 figure describes the diabetes task only; it does not generalise to other conditions.
- Not yet implemented: trained models for heart disease, stroke, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, asthma and COPD. These are roadmap items — no model exists for them today.

## Pages

- [Welcome](https://whyrisk.vercel.app/welcome): what WhyRisk is, what is real today, and what is roadmap.
- [Model card](https://whyrisk.vercel.app/model-card): the model's dataset, measured performance, live service status, and limitations, stated in full.

## Disclaimer

WhyRisk is an experimental clinical decision-support and research tool. It is not a certified medical device and is not a substitute for professional medical diagnosis, treatment, or clinical judgment. Predictions must be reviewed by qualified healthcare professionals.
